title: Synthetic-region failback controller for Private VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a controller and IaC orchestration that can run repeatable, auditable failover and failback drills for Private (VPC) deployments across multiple regions. The controller should synthesize Terraform actions, coordinate DNS/route updates, warm KV caches and model caches in target regions, gate traffic shifts on health checks, and produce a post-drill report. This ticket covers the controller PoC, the Terraform module wiring for orchestration, health-check gating rules, and the first two synthetic regional drills against staging clusters.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A single CLI subcommand (redwoodctl driller run --plan=<plan>) executes a pre-defined synthetic failover plan against staging VPCs and completes without manual intervention.
2) Traffic shift is gated by health checks (application-level readiness, KV warm, embedding latency) and will not exceed 20% incremental weight per 5 minutes unless explicitly overridden.
3) Full failback can be executed and completes within 30 minutes of initiating rollback, with state reconciled to pre-drill baseline.
4) All IaC actions are captured as Terraform plan/apply artifacts and stored in S3 with audit metadata.
5) Dashboard shows timeline, tokenized cost delta, and customer-impact flag for the drill.
6) No production customer data leaves the target VPCs during the drill and audit logs are recorded to the central audit cluster.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (PoC): implement a small controller service (Go) that accepts a JSON 'drill plan' and translates to a sequence of Terraform operations (plan -> apply), DNS weighted-change, and validation hooks. Wire controller to existing terraform modules for Private deployment (reuse module outputs for cluster endpoints). Implement health-check webhooks and basic circuit-breaker gating.
Phase 2: extend Plan DSL to allow canary increments, KV cache warmup jobs, model variant pinning for the duration of the drill, and automatic rollback. Add RBAC and audit metadata.
Phase 3: run 2 scheduled drills in staging and one shadow drill in a subset of production-like Private deployments, collect metrics, and iterate on timings.
Note: use a dedicated state bucket per drill to avoid cross-plan state interference. Apply only to staging clusters until security review complete.
terraform_modules: private/drill-orchestrator (new) - composes cross-region resources and S3 plan storage
network/routing (tweaks) - small helper to rotate route-table priorities
ci_pipeline: drill-ci (pipe runs terraform fmt, plan, controller unit tests, e2e in staging namespace)
health_checks: kv-cache-warm - background job verifies >90% hit rate on warmup prefix
embedding-latency - 95th percentile under configured SLO for 5m
rollback_strategy: Automated rollback triggered if any gating health-check fails after a traffic shift step. Rollback starts by reverting DNS weight to previous values, then tearing down any ephemeral infra (warmup jobs), and finally running terraform apply with the saved rollback plan. All steps logged and a human-in-loop approval required if repeated rollback occurs within 1 hour.
tests: unit: controller action translation (mock terraform) - local
integration: run drill plan against staging (isolated VPC) - nightly
chaos: synthetic API latency injected during canary to validate rollback gating - one-off
notes: Trade-offs discussed: 1) We will not attempt live DB cross-region replication for failover in this ticket; the scope is network/routing, DNS, and application-level failover for stateless inference nodes. 2) Using Terraform CLI for orchestration reduces initial dev time but means coerced state management; mitigation: isolate state buckets per drill and keep apply windows short. 3) We debated adopting Terragrunt; decided to postpone to avoid adding another toolchain until PoC proves value.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Raman: Initial ticket filed. Proposal includes a small controller to orchestrate terraform + routing + health gates. Linked PoC design doc on Confluence.

2026-02-24 - Liang Chen (infra reviewer): Prefer explicit per-drill state bucket. Raised concern about Terraform apply side effects on long-lived modules. Suggested adding 'dry-run' simulation mode and immutable plan snapshots.

2026-02-28 - Evan Schultz: Implemented controller skeleton and a 'dry-run -> plan snapshot' flow in controller. Pushed initial code to github PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controller/pull/118. Unit tests passing locally.

2026-03-02 - Marta Ruiz (Security): Flagged audit logging requirement and asked for KMS-encrypted S3 artifacts. Also requested a short threat model for the drill that will be reviewed in next security sync.

2026-03-05 - Evan Schultz: Added S3 encryption and minimal audit metadata. Created draft threat model and posted to Confluence. Running the first synthetic drill in a staging namespace next week. CI job 'drill-ci' created: runs terraform plan and controller e2e.

2026-03-10 - QA Lead (Rina Patel): Nightly integration run observed a timing flake: KV warmup sometimes exceeds 7 minutes at cold-start. Suggested adding parallel warmup workers and a warmup-timeout gating metric. Created follow-up ticket idea for optimizing warmup (ENG-28210).
post_drill_report_template: S3 URL to store: s3://redwood-drill-reports/<drill-id>/report.json. Must include: timeline, terraform plan diffs, pre/post metrics (latency, error-rate, cost delta), gates triggered, rollback events, and recommended follow-ups.
audit_requirements: All plan/apply artifacts, controller actions, CLI invocations must be logged with user, timestamp, and drill-id. S3 artifacts must be encrypted with CMK 'projects/private-drill-cmk'. Console dashboard must show drill as 'simulated' if run in staging.
